chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from 'Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, who said:

I was present at al-Bayt al-Haram, and a man was calling out to Abu Ja'far al-Mansur while he was performing tawaf, saying: O Commander of the Faithful, these two men came to my brother by night and took him out of his home, and he did not return to me. By Allah, I do not know what they did with him. Abu Ja'far said to them: What did you do with him? They said: O Commander of the Faithful, we spoke with him, then he returned to his home. He said to them: Meet me tomorrow at salat al-'asr in this place.

So they met him the next day at salat al-'asr and brought him there. He said to Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, while holding his hand: O Ja'far, judge between them. He said: O Commander of the Faithful, you judge between them. He said to him: By my right over you, you must judge between them. He said: So Ja'far عليه السلام came out, and a reed prayer-mat was spread for him, and he sat upon it. Then the litigants came and sat before him. He said: What do you say? He said: O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, these two came to my brother by night and took him out of his home. By Allah, he did not return to me, and by Allah, I do not know what they did with him. He said: What do you two say? They said: O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, we spoke with him, then he returned to his home.

Then Ja'far عليه السلام said: O servant, write: In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Whoever comes to a man by night and takes him out of his home is liable for him unless he establishes proof that he returned him to his home. O servant, move this one aside and strike his neck. He said: O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, by Allah, I did not kill him; rather, I held him, then this one came and stabbed him and killed him. He said: I am the son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم; O servant, move this one aside and strike the neck of the other. He said: By Allah, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, by Allah, I did not torture him, but I killed him with a single blow.

So he ordered regarding the brother, and his neck was struck. Then he ordered regarding the other, and his sides were beaten, and he was imprisoned. And he wrote over his case: He is to be imprisoned for his lifetime and given fifty lashes every year.

key_terms.اقْضِ: judge or decide the case judicially
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: the prison or place of confinement
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةَ: legal proof or evidence establishing a claim
key_terms.الْبَيْتِ الْحَرَامِ: the Sacred House, the sanctuary of the Ka'bah in Makkah
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for the person taken

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who takes a man out of his home at night and he disappears or is killed?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a judicial case in which Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام judged between litigants concerning a man taken from his home at night and killed. It establishes a legal principle from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم that whoever removes a person from his home by night is liable for him unless he proves that he returned him safely. The report also demonstrates the Imam’s judicial authority and the application of liability and punishment in homicide-related cases.
